name: Push-ups
description: A classic bodyweight exercise that targets the chest, shoulders, and triceps. Start in a plank position with hands shoulder-width apart, lower your body until your chest nearly touches the floor, then push back up.
tips: Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels
Engage your core throughout the movement
Lower yourself until your elbows form a 90-degree angle
For beginners, try doing push-ups on your knees

name: Squats
description: A fundamental lower body exercise that targets the quadriceps, hamstrings, and glutes. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, lower your body by bending your knees and pushing your hips back, then return to standing.
tips: Keep your chest up and back straight
Push your knees outward as you descend
Lower until your thighs are parallel to the ground
Keep your weight on your heels

name: Plank
description: An isometric core exercise that strengthens the abdominals, back, and shoulders. Hold a position similar to a push-up, but with your weight on your forearms.
tips: Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels
Engage your core and glutes
Don't let your hips sag or pike up
Focus on breathing steadily throughout the hold

name: Lunges
description: A unilateral lower body exercise that targets the quadriceps, hamstrings, and glutes. Step forward with one leg, lowering your body until both knees form 90-degree angles, then push back to the starting position.
tips: Keep your upper body straight and shoulders back
Step forward far enough that your knee doesn't extend past your toes
Lower your body until both knees form 90-degree angles
Push through the heel of your front foot to return to standing

name: Burpees
description: A full-body exercise that combines a squat, push-up, and jump. Begin in a standing position, drop into a squat, kick your feet back into a plank, perform a push-up, jump your feet back to the squat position, and explosively jump up.
tips: Focus on form rather than speed, especially when beginning
Modify by stepping back instead of jumping if needed
Keep your core engaged throughout the movement
Land softly when jumping to protect your joints

name: Pull-ups
description: An upper body exercise that targets the back, biceps, and shoulders. Hang from a bar with palms facing away from you, then pull your body up until your chin is over the bar.
tips: Start from a dead hang with arms fully extended
Pull your shoulder blades down and back before pulling up
Try to get your chin over the bar
Lower yourself with control

name: Dips
description: An upper body exercise that targets the triceps, chest, and shoulders. Support your body between parallel bars or on the edge of a bench, lower your body by bending your elbows, then push back up.
tips: Keep your elbows close to your body for more triceps focus
Lean forward slightly for more chest engagement
Lower until your elbows form a 90-degree angle
For beginners, use a bench and keep your feet on the ground

name: Mountain Climbers
description: A dynamic exercise that targets the core, shoulders, and hip flexors while providing cardiovascular benefits. Start in a plank position and alternate bringing your knees toward your chest in a running motion.
tips: Keep your hips level and don't let them rise up
Engage your core throughout the movement
Move at a controlled pace to maintain form
Breathe rhythmically with your movements

name: Deadlifts
description: A compound exercise that targets the hamstrings, glutes, lower back, and traps. Stand with feet hip-width apart, bend at the hips and knees to grasp a barbell, then stand up straight while keeping the barbell close to your body.
tips: Keep your back straight and chest up throughout the movement
Push through your heels as you lift
Keep the weight close to your body
Engage your core to protect your lower back

name: Russian Twists
description: A rotational exercise that targets the obliques and abdominals. Sit on the floor with knees bent, lean back slightly, lift your feet off the ground, and twist your torso from side to side.
tips: Keep your back straight, not rounded
Twist from your core, not your arms
For added difficulty, hold a weight or medicine ball
Keep your feet elevated throughout the movement for more challenge
